findings.title: French assistance and the choice of commercial alliance
findings.payer: French Crown, routed through Beaumarchais and Roderigue Hortalez and Company
findings.measurement: Initial covert support described by Library of Congress; institutional historical synthesis, not a newly reconciled payment ledger
findings.mechanism: American need for overseas military supplies shaped negotiations over commercial terms and alliance. Congress adopted the Model Treaty on September 17, 1776; agreements with France followed in 1778.
findings.policy_instrument: Model Treaty of 1776 and Franco-American commercial/alliance treaties of 1778
findings.outcome: Financing and diplomacy interacted. This is foreign state support of the Revolution, not domestic campaign finance or proof of a purchased vote.
findings.evidence_strength: Institutional historical synthesis linking finance, procurement and diplomacy; exact accounting status disputed in historical records.
findings.counterevidence: The State Department history records disagreement over whether early aid was a gift or loan. France also pursued strategic interests against Britain. Do not add repeated descriptions of the same funds or assume a dollar conversion.

lineage.actor_role: Vergennes: French foreign minister; Beaumarchais: commercial intermediary; American commissioners negotiated assistance.
lineage.continuity_boundary: Specific state-credit and treaty relationship, not evidence of an unbroken secret control structure through 2026.
